content:
{
  "root_cause": "The tabbable function in src/index.js incorrectly orders elements with positive tabindex before those with tabindex zero or omitted, deviating from the HTML tabindex specification. This can cause the focus-trap's initial focus logic to select the wrong element when such tabindex values are present, and in the tested scenario contributes to the perception of delayed focus movement due to the focus-trap's default delayInitialFocus behavior.",
  "repair_strategy": "Replace the tabbable function with a simpler implementation that returns focusable candidates in document order, ignoring tabindex ordering. This ensures the first focusable element in the DOM (the #street input) is selected as the initial focus node when the dialog opens, aligning with the expected behavior for keyboard users.",
  "expected_accessibility_effect": "Keyboard users will receive focus on the first usable field (#street input) when the address dialog opens, satisfying WCAG 2.1.1 (Keyboard) and 2.4.3 (Focus Order).",
  "functional_risks": [
    "Components that rely on explicit positive tabindex values for custom focus order may experience altered tab order. However, the application under test does not use positive tabindex values, so the risk is low for this deployment."
  ],
  "verification_requirements": [
    "Verify that pressing Enter to open the dialog moves focus to the #street input.",
    "Verify that typing a street address and pressing Save updates the status correctly and hides the dialog.",
    "Verify that pressing Escape closes the dialog and returns focus to the #open button.",
    "Verify that tab navigation within the dialog follows document order for elements with tabindex zero or omitted, and that any existing positive tabindex values continue to be respected (though none are present in the current UI)."
  ]
}
